claims.text: Oden is simmered in a shared soy-and-dashi broth and the menu includes wheat-fried/breaded items (fried tofu, burdock tempura, skewered cutlets), so gluten exposure and cross-contact are likely.
Oden broth is soy-sauce and dashi based; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat and no gluten-free alternative is indicated.
Vegetable items such as tofu, daikon and burdock are cooked in the same fish/bonito dashi oden pot used for meat and fish items, so they are not vegan.
Burgers are served on wheat buns and the shop is a bread-and-meat operation; no gluten-free preparation or separation is advertised.
The signature beef burger is finished with a house-made smoked soy sauce; Japanese soy sauce normally contains wheat, so it is not gluten-free.
The kitchen centers on house-smoked bacon, ham, sausage and beef patties, so shared grill/equipment cross-contact with animal products is highly likely for any meat-free item.
The menu page includes an allergen information sheet, indicating the shop documents allergens for its dishes.
An allergen information chart is provided on the menu, so diners with allergies can review ingredient information on site.
No gluten-free handling documented; menu includes wheat noodles (nyūmen/sōmen), sushi, and sandwiches, so shared surfaces and wheat exposure are likely.
Sushi and dashi-based noodle broths are on the menu; standard Japanese soy sauce and broths contain wheat, and no wheat-free versions are documented.
Kitchen prepares chicken, mackerel, and beef dishes; no vegan-dedicated preparation is documented, so cross-contact with animal products is likely.
Some plant-forward items appear on the menu, including a Yamato vegetable smoothie, herbal/Yamato teas, and anmitsu-style sweets, giving vegetarians a few options to ask about.
Wheat noodles (Miwa somen and udon) are core menu items prepared in the same kitchen, so flour and gluten are pervasive; no gluten-free handling is documented.

The restaurant explicitly offers a shojin-style signature set that excludes meat, egg and dairy, making a plant-based meal genuinely available.

As a classic Chinese kitchen, dishes rely heavily on regular (wheat-based) soy sauce and seasonings.
Signature dishes use pork, shrimp and crab, and stocks/sauces are meat- and fish-based, with no separate vegan preparation noted.

name: 七福食堂／喫茶古白 (Shichifuku Shokudo / Kissa Kohaku)

claims.text: Lunch sets regularly include wheat-based items (tempura, chilled wheat noodles, miso-glazed fu/seitan), so wheat is handled throughout the small kitchen.
Dishes use standard Japanese seasonings (soy sauce, miso glaze) which contain wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.
The menu is meat- and fish-centered (pork hotpot, shrimp chirashi, mozuku) and most dishes use fish dashi, so vegan separation is not maintained.
Cooking emphasizes seasonal local and Yamato/Nara-area vegetables (e.g. produce from a farm in Ikoma), so plant-forward side dishes are part of the meal even though they are not certified vegan.

name: 鹿の舟 竈 (Shika no Fune Kamado)

claims.text: Meals are built on miso, soy sauce, and tofu, and at least one set (Yamato beef hot pot) includes wheat gluten (fu), so wheat is present across the standard menu.
Menus rotate and include meat (Yamato beef) and fish-based items alongside vegetable and tofu dishes, so a strictly vegan meal is not guaranteed and would need to be confirmed per day.
The venue lists allergy accommodations available upon consultation and offers an English menu.
The miso soup and base preparations use a kombu-based dashi rather than fish dashi, making a vegetable-and-tofu-centered meal realistic for those avoiding fish stock.
Cooking centers on local Yamato vegetables, tofu, and kamado-cooked rice, so plant-forward options are a core part of the menu.

name: 鹿の舟 囀 (Shika no Fune Saezuri)

claims.text: Wheat is central to the menu (campagne-bread toasts, cakes), so heavy gluten presence and cross-contact in a small café kitchen should be assumed.
Signature desserts use homemade custard cream and vanilla ice cream (dairy/egg), so dessert prep surfaces are not vegan-isolated.
Organic Yamato tea from Nara's Tsukigase region is available and is naturally gluten-free and vegan as a drink.
Desserts emphasize whole seasonal fruit, so a fresh-fruit option may be available for restricted diners — ask on the day.
